summary: Post-imaging NVMe power-state change causes failed suspend/resume and accelerated battery drain
description: After the recent corporate image (win-provision-2026.03) was applied to a subset of new workstations, several users reported devices failing to resume from suspend and exhibiting rapid battery drain while idle. Symptoms started appearing post-imaging and are reproducible on affected hardware. This ticket tracks triage, root cause investigation, and remediation steps.
impact: ~9 devices affected in us-east fleet. Users report lost work and devices hot while idle; several devices reached battery <10% within 6 hours when expected idle drain is <2%.
steps_to_reproduce: Apply win-provision-2026.03 corporate image to stock device (fresh out-of-box) following standard autopilot flow
Boot to Windows 11 22H2 with corporate OOBE scripts and Intune MDM enrollment
Allow device to idle for 10 minutes, then close lid to trigger suspend
Open lid after 5-15 minutes; device either fails to restore display and input, or resumes with fan spin and NVMe temperature elevated
Observe battery level over 4-6 hours while device remains idle at login screen
logs: Attached: kernel-power.evtx snippets from affected devices showing multiple DPC watchdog warnings around suspend/resume
PowerCfg energy-report HTML shows unexpected runtime active time and disk activity from "storahci" and NVMe driver during idle
Windows Event IDs: 42 (sleep), 41 (kernel-power) correlated with time of failed resume on 3 devices
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: recent NVMe driver or AHCI/storahci policy in the image is preventing proper power state entry (D3) and leaving the controller active
Checked imaging bundles: win-provision-2026.03 included vendor NVMe driver 3.1.0.12 and a custom power plan XML that tweaks device wake timers
Reproduced failure on two lab units; captured kernel stack traces showing storport/NVMe IO queued during suspend path
SCCM/driver catalog shows vendor driver replaced earlier this month from 2.9.0.x => 3.1.0.12; rollback to 2.9.0.45 in lab resolved suspend/resume on one unit
No network activity expected during deep sleep; pcap from one device shows periodic NVMe telemetry queries from vendor service (nvme_telemetry.exe) running under SYSTEM after imaging
Autopilot log confirms image applied successfully; no custom scheduled tasks were added except vendor telemetry service installed by driver package
comments: Aisha Patel (reporter) - 2026-03-10: First report received via #internal-it from onboarding queue; user device hot to touch after lid reopen. Started ticket.
Diego Ramos (assignee) - 2026-03-11: Reproduced on spare Dell 7440; collected kernel dumps and energy report. Suspicion on vendor NVMe driver.
SRE (Maya Chen) - 2026-03-11: Can you share driver package ID and vendor service entries? We can block service via AppLocker if needed as interim.
Diego Ramos - 2026-03-12: Rolled back NVMe driver to 2.9.0.45 on two lab units — suspend/resume restored; battery drain stopped. Created imaging test image with older driver.
Security (Omar Khalid) - 2026-03-12: Vendor telemetry executable flagged in EDR policy baseline; suggest hold for exec-level decision before mass rollback on fleet.
Diego Ramos - 2026-03-13: Preparing hotfix imaging bundle and rollback playbook for SOC-approved drivers. Scheduling limited pilot for affected devices.
resolution_notes: Workaround: For affected devices, rollback NVMe driver to vendor version 2.9.0.45 or disable vendor NVMe telemetry service. Both approaches restored suspend/resume and eliminated elevated idle disk activity in lab tests.

Planned remediation: Publish urgent imaging hotfix (win-provision-2026.03-rollback-nvme) removing 3.1.0.12 driver and pinning to 2.9.0.45. Disable telemetry service via service startmode=disabled in image. Deploy to pilot group of 25 devices in us-east tomorrow morning.
Change control: RFC submitted to change board with risk assessment; Security has requested an exception/whitepaper on vendor telemetry before fleet-wide deploy.
Postmortem action: Add driver-version gating to imaging pipeline and automate kernel power regression tests (suspend/resume, energy-report) in preflight for every new image.
suggested_fix: Create and publish hotfix imaging bundle that pins NVMe driver to 2.9.0.45 and disables vendor telemetry service; run a 48-hour pilot on 25 devices, confirm energy reports and kernel-power events are normal, then roll out to remaining affected fleet.
follow_up_actions: Automate suspend/resume regression tests in CI for imaging pipeline
Add driver whitelisting and version pin checks to SCCM driver catalog sync
Coordinate with Security to evaluate vendor telemetry; request vendor engineering notes for driver 3.1.x changes
Notify Fleet Ops and create KB for helpdesk with rollback Playbook and AppLocker rule to block telemetry if immediate fix needed
